description: This article-linked C++ library traces mutually connected components as nodes or links are removed from interdependent network layers. Its contributors provide a header-only implementation, example programs and tests so modellers can compute a key state in network-percolation simulations. Inputs are layered network connections and decremental changes; outputs are the components that remain mutually connected across the layers. The software has no built-in place, observation period or spatial resolution: each property follows the network supplied by the user. Source is public under MIT, with C++11 and Boost.Optional required to compile it. A modeller could use the component to simulate cascading disconnection between electricity, telecommunications or other dependent infrastructure networks. The article discusses catastrophic failures and percolation, but no named asset network is included in the material reviewed here. Results are connectivity states, not direct estimates of service loss or restoration time. No related catalogue record was identified. The code was not compiled, timed or run against an infrastructure network. The resource format is C++ header source, available directly from the public GitHub repository.
